items.title: Section: Two Causes of Right View, and Why Cessation Has No Counterpart

items.zh: 正見因緣，當知即是有佛出世、聽聞正法、無倒思惟。又出世間正見果相，當知即是前後常故，無所對故。若法，所治若有，生已無滅；所治若無，滅已有生，彼法名有所對。若法，所治若有若無、若生不生，常時是有，彼法名無所對。
items.en: The cause of right view is a buddha's appearance in the world, hearing the true Dharma, and correct reflection without distortion. The fruit-characteristic of transcendent right view is remaining constant before and after, without any counterpart. A phenomenon that, while the affliction it counteracts still exists, arises and continues without ceasing, or once that affliction is exhausted, having ceased then arises anew, has a counterpart. A phenomenon that remains constantly existent regardless of whether the affliction it counteracts exists or not, or whether the corresponding wisdom has arisen or not, has no counterpart.

items.title: Section: Mind as the Newspaper's Editor, and Why a Lamp's Flame Depends on Its Own Light

items.zh: 又即此果，由心解脫增上力故，於自所行及彼所依得清淨者，當知即是由清淨心增上力故，於諸色根所行境界不生雜染，及令諸根順清淨故。又解脫心住者，當知即是壽之與煖展轉相依相屬而住。
items.en: This same fruit, through the enhancing power of mind-liberation, achieves purity in the field of activity proper to the sense faculties and in what they depend upon, which is, through the enhancing power of a purified mind, that the physical sense faculties no longer give rise to defilement towards their objects, and every faculty is brought into accord with purity. The abiding of the liberated mind should be known as life force and warmth sustaining one another in turn.

items.title: Section: Ignorance That Breeds Rebirth, Wisdom That Ends It

items.zh: 又此世間及出世間二種解脫果差別者，當知即是於諸受中及因緣中，有癡愛者後有當生，無癡愛者後有不生。
items.en: The difference between the fruit of the mundane and the transcendent kinds of liberation is this: among the feelings and their causes and conditions, one in whom delusion and craving remain will give rise to future existence; one in whom delusion and craving are absent will not give rise to future existence.

items.title: Section: A Second Meaning of the Fruit's Difference, and Six Kinds of Stillness Begin

items.zh: 又彼相雜而相應故，彼能依止心法清淨，當知即是非現在緣之所染污領受彼故。即二解脫住差別者，當知即是六寂靜故。由清淨識沒平等故，非由彼所依平等故。
items.en: The mundane fruit remains intermixed and associated with affliction. The dependent mental factors of the transcendent fruit are purified, meaning it is not stained by present objects while receiving them. The difference in how these two liberations abide should be known through six kinds of stillness. Through the even subsiding of purified consciousness, not through the even subsiding of the faculties it depends upon.

items.title: Section: Entering and Leaving Without Effort, Stillness Even in the Body's Own Activity

items.zh: 於入定時，不由加行入寂靜故。於出定時，不由加行出寂靜故，次第出故。於在定時，三行不行得寂靜故。
items.en: Upon entering, stillness is achieved without effortful application. Upon emerging, stillness is achieved without effortful application, emerging in sequence. While remaining within the attainment, stillness is achieved through the three kinds of activity ceasing to function.

items.title: Section: A Mind Kept Still Whether Among Companions or Crowds

items.zh: 於遠離出心寂靜故，謂於三時。一、於阿練若，與同梵行共相雜住；二、於聚落中，與諸在家共相雜住；三、於二處行相現行。
items.en: Stillness of mind upon leaving solitude is found across three occasions. First, dwelling in the wilderness together with fellow practitioners of pure conduct. Second, dwelling in a village together with householders. Third, activity in either of the two settings, wherever one dwells among others.

items.title: Section: Three Touches Felt on Returning from the Deepest Stillness

items.zh: 於親近出心寂靜故，謂於三時。一、於有色世間勝定出故；二、於無色世間勝定出故；三、於出世間有心定出故。又此諸定非唯滅定出已方得，亦先已得，今起現前。
items.en: Stillness of mind in what immediately adjoins emergence is found across three occasions: emerging into a supreme worldly concentration still possessing form; emerging into a supreme worldly concentration without form; and emerging into a transcendent concentration still possessing mind. These concentrations are not necessarily newly attained only upon emerging from cessation; they may already have been attained before, and now simply arise again in the present.

items.title: Section: How a Concentration with Signs Differs from One Without

items.zh: 此中前二，由次第定故，展轉獲得勝定清淨。後一，不由次第定故，然由通達無相界故，展轉獲得勝定清淨。又有相定，由有相作意，入、住、出定。若無相定，由無相作意入定、住定；由有相作意，當知出定。
items.en: Among these, the first two are attained progressively through successive concentration, gradually achieving the purity of supreme concentration. The last is not attained progressively, but through penetrating the signless realm, gradually achieving the purity of supreme concentration in that way. A concentration possessing signs is entered, dwelt within, and left through mental application possessing signs. A signless concentration is entered and dwelt within through signless mental application; one should know it is left through mental application possessing signs.

items.title: Section: A Third Sutra Opens with Eight Aspects for Asking the Dharma Rightly

items.zh: 復次，當釋法因緣經。謂於阿毘達摩、阿毘毘奈耶中，善巧苾芻、或鄔波索迦，欲依解了而請問者，當依八相而興請問。何等八相？謂解了事、解了所治、解了果、解了自性、解了果差別、解了所依、解了功德、解了證得。
items.en: The Sutra of the Causes and Conditions of the Dharma shall now be explained. A skilful monk or lay devotee wishing to inquire in order to gain understanding of the higher teaching and the higher discipline, should frame the inquiry through eight aspects. What are the eight? Understanding the matter, understanding what is to be overcome, understanding the result, understanding the essential nature, understanding the distinction of results, understanding the basis, understanding the virtues, and understanding the realisation.

items.title: Section: The Five Aggregates, Two Defilements, and the Noble Eightfold Path

items.zh: 解了事者，謂能解了五取蘊故。解了所治者，謂愛雜染及見雜染。由愛雜染故，於後有滅不生欣樂。由見雜染故，雖生欣樂而不能證。解了果者，謂此三種雜染永斷。解了自性者，謂八聖支道。
items.en: Understanding the matter is understanding the five aggregates of clinging. Understanding what is to be overcome is the defilement of craving and the defilement of view. Through the defilement of craving, one does not delight in the cessation of future existence. Through the defilement of view, even while delighting in it, one cannot realise it. Understanding the result is the permanent severing of these two defilements. Understanding the essential nature is the noble eightfold path.

items.title: Section: Three Aggregates Behind Eight Path-Factors, and the Fruits of Severing Defilement

items.zh: 此復種種差別宣說。對治外道諸邪道故，名八聖支道。對治三種雜染故，建立三蘊。謂對治惡行雜染故、對治諸欲雜染故、對治諸見雜染故。是出世間有為所攝。解了果差別者，謂諸斷滅。是出世間無為所攝。
items.en: This is explained through various distinctions. It is called the noble eightfold path because it counters every wrong path of non-Buddhist teachings. Three aggregates are established to counter three kinds of defilement: countering the defilement of unwholesome conduct, countering the defilement of desire, and countering the defilement of views. This belongs to the transcendent conditioned. Understanding the distinction of results is the various kinds of severing. This belongs to the transcendent unconditioned.

items.title: Section: Concentration's Own Lineage, Signs, Objects, and Requisites

items.zh: 解了所依者，謂三摩地。此復四種應知。一、由種姓故，謂所有定一切皆由靜慮種姓，隨所宣說諸靜慮支皆能解了。二、由相故。三、由生所緣相故。四、由成辦因緣相故。
items.en: Understanding the basis is understanding concentration itself, which should be known through four further aspects. First, by way of lineage, all concentration belongs to the lineage of meditative absorption, through which every stated factor of absorption can be understood. Second, by way of characteristic. Third, by way of the object giving rise to it. Fourth, by way of the causes and conditions that accomplish it.

items.title: Section: What the Buddha Himself First Contemplated About Feeling

items.zh: 解了功德者，謂滅盡定最第一住，說名解了功德。當知此相復有五種。謂滅事故、寂靜相似影像故、入定因緣故、出定因緣故、出定功德故。解了證得者，謂於五取蘊，以八種相觀察諸受。謂觀察自性、觀察現法轉因緣、觀察現法轉滅因緣、觀察當來轉因緣、觀察彼二轉滅因緣、觀察轉因緣因緣、觀察還因緣因緣，及觀察還。
items.en: Understanding the virtues is understanding that the cessation attainment is the foremost among abidings. Understanding the realisation is observing feeling across the five aggregates of clinging through eight aspects: observing its nature, the cause of its present arising, the cause of its present cessation, the cause of its future arising, the cause of its future cessation, the cause of that arising-cause, the cause of that cessation-cause, and observing release from it.

items.zh: 此中樂俱行對治，謂於最勝根本靜慮；苦俱行對治，謂得近分出離欲俱行；不苦不樂俱行對治，謂即於根本靜慮。為欲顯示轉因緣滅故，即依諸受說所有受皆悉是苦。由彼三受約第一義皆是苦故。

blocks.text: Right view, the stillness of cessation, and the three "touches" on returning from it.
Master Cháng Bǎi: without a buddha's appearance, beings would never know the four truths; right view arises through hearing and correct reflection. Cessation is unconditioned.
Master Cháng Bǎi: life force, the life faculty, and warmth rely on one another, even in one resting in cessation.
Master Cháng Bǎi: with ignorance and craving uncut, karma is made and suffering comes; when they are cut, suffering ends.

Master Cháng Bǎi: the six consciousnesses and their factors cease to manifest; the faculties remain. Having cultivated it much, one enters and leaves spontaneously; whether in wilderness or a crowded village, the mind stays still.
Master Cháng Bǎi: leaving cessation, the sage passes into form, formless, or undefiled concentration.

Master Cháng Bǎi: the worldly concentrations come from the nine successive stages; the transcendent one comes from penetrating reality. If a mental application with signs arises, one has left signless concentration.
Master Cháng Bǎi: when asking for teaching, rely on eight aspects. The five aggregates are the root; the precepts aggregate counters wrong conduct, concentration counters desire, wisdom severs.
Master Cháng Bǎi: whoever wishes to leave birth and death must rely on concentration and cultivate insight.

Master Cháng Bǎi: only by cutting self-grasping ignorance, acquired and innate, can one finally leave feelings behind. (Untranslated, 0647c22: pleasant feelings are countered by root meditation, painful by renunciation at the threshold; all feelings are suffering in the ultimate sense.)
Stillness "even in a crowded village": the treatise's highest meditation is not escape from the world.

quiz.q: What does the treatise give as the causes of right view?
options: pure precepts, solitude, and meditation, right view being born only from concentration, as the text says
noble birth, good health, and long life
giving, precepts, and heavenly rebirth
a buddha's appearance, hearing the true Dharma, and correct reflection without distortion
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: without a buddha's appearance, beings would never know good and evil causes, the four truths, or how to practise; through hearing and undistorted reflection right view is gained. All three causes come from outside and within together.

quiz.q: 所治若有 is rendered "once the affliction it corresponds to still exists." What is lost, per the lecture?
options: the relation of antidote and what is overcome, so the test for having a counterpart disappears
nothing: it means associated, right view arising with affliction, as the lecture says, so the sense is kept
it loses the hypothetical mood of 若有
it loses 生已無滅
quiz.why: The lecture treats right view as the antidote and afflictions as what is overcome. Master Cháng Bǎi: transcendent right view is conditioned and undefiled, hence with a counterpart; the nirvana it realises is unconditioned, without one. "Corresponds to" hides this.

quiz.q: What does the treatise say the abiding of the liberated mind is?
options: consciousness and name-and-form sustaining one another, as in dependent origination
life force and warmth sustaining one another in turn
mind and mental factors abiding in association
the meditations and formless states abiding in sequence
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: this means life force, the life faculty, and warmth rely on and belong to one another so as to abide. He applies this to one resting in the cessation of feeling and perception, while the treatise states only the mutual dependence.

quiz.q: How do the fruits of the mundane and transcendent liberations differ?
options: mundane fruit brings human or heavenly birth and transcendent the pure lands, both still with future lives, differing only in place
with delusion and craving, future existence arises; with their seeds cut, one leaves the three realms for good
mundane fruit has no feeling, transcendent has feeling
mundane fruit has no conditions, transcendent has them
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: with seeds of ignorance and craving uncut, afflictions rise, karma is made, and suffering comes in the next life. When they are cut, at feeling no affliction or karma arises, and one leaves the three realms.

quiz.q: Why can one enter and leave without effort, and what is the stillness within, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: much practice makes entry and exit spontaneous; within it the three activities stop, a stillness like nirvana
the Buddha's power brings it, and subtle thought remains within
the one who enters is an arhat
the power comes from past karma
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: having cultivated this attainment very much, one enters and leaves spontaneously. Within it bodily, verbal, and mental activities stop, with no breath, no speech, and no thinking, attaining a stillness like nirvana.

quiz.q: This is rendered "the activity of both settings occurring together." What is the problem?
options: none: one is in both places at once by a power, as the lecture explains, so the wording is exact
二處 should mean heaven and earth
二處 should mean in and out of meditation
it means either setting, stillness holding wherever one is, not both at once
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: whether in quiet wilderness or a crowded village, dwelling with others, the mind stays still without worldly distraction. The 《披尋記》 speaks of an unfixed situation. So the third covers either place, not both happening together.

quiz.q: What are the three occasions of the nearest exit?
options: in the wilderness, in a village, and in either, the three shared with leaving solitude
into supreme worldly concentration with form, without form, and transcendent concentration with mind
on entering, on abiding, and on leaving
the first, middle, and last watches of the night
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: leaving cessation, the sage goes step by step or directly into form concentration, formless concentration, or undefiled concentration with mind, and is still in all three. Wilderness and village belong to the previous item, leaving through solitude.

quiz.q: How do the first two concentrations differ from the last in how they are gained?
options: the first two through the signless realm, and the last through the nine stages, being their summit
all three through successive stages
all three through the signless realm
the first two come through the nine successive stages, and the last through penetrating the signless realm
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the two worldly concentrations come from practising the nine successive stages; the transcendent one comes not by sequence but from penetrating the signless realm, not attending to any sign. The treatise's "first two" and "last" refer back to §40.

quiz.q: How does one leave signless concentration, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: entering, abiding, and leaving all by signless application, signs never arising
if a mental application with signs arises within it, one has thereby left the concentration
one must be awakened by someone else
it ends by itself when the time is up
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: if a mental application with signs arises in signless concentration, know that through this one has left it. So entering and abiding are signless, while leaving involves signs. This contrasts with concentration with signs, where all three have signs.

quiz.q: This is rendered "wishing to inquire, with real understanding." What is the error in sense?
options: none: only one who already understands can ask, as the lecture sees it
it should be "wishing to teach"
it should be "without understanding"
one inquires in order to understand, whereas the English has the inquirer already understanding
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: wishing to understand the meaning of the Buddha's teaching or how to practise, when requesting the Dharma, one should rely on the eight aspects. So understanding is the aim of the question and not its precondition.

quiz.q: The eightfold path sets up three aggregates to counter which three defilements?
options: the defilements of affliction, karma, and birth, the treatise's usual three
the defilements of unwholesome conduct, of desire, and of views
the defilements of greed, hatred, and delusion
the defilements of body, speech, and mind
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the aggregate of precepts counters evil conduct, with right speech, action, and livelihood; the aggregate of meditation counters desire, with right mindfulness and concentration. The usual three defilements are a different list from the one here.

quiz.q: What is understanding the basis, and through how many aspects is it known?
options: cessation, known through entering, abiding, and leaving, the highest concentration being the basis
concentration, known through lineage, characteristic, the object producing it, and the causes accomplishing it
the five aggregates, known through their five divisions
the eightfold path, known through its three trainings
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: whoever wishes to leave birth and death or attain awakening must rely on concentration and cultivate insight. That explains why concentration is the basis. Cessation appears under virtues, which is the next item.

quiz.q: The third and eighth aspects both use "cessation" in English. What is the problem?
options: the third concerns cessation, while 還 in the eighth is escape, so a distinction among the eight is lost
none: 還 means cessation, the treatise dividing it only to reach eight
the third should be "arising"
the eighth should be "return to the world"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: only by cutting self-grasping ignorance, both acquired and innate, can one finally depart from feelings. 還 concerns this departure, so "escape" or "departure" would keep it apart from the third aspect's cessation.
